description: Unit: resolveChargeProfile returns the correct profile and source for each of the five chain steps in isolation.
Unit: resolveChargeProfile always terminates at the client default and never returns null, including when every upstream assignment is absent.
Unit: precedence property — a contract-line or contract profile assignment always wins over a conflicting work-item assignment.
Unit: an explicit profile on the source record wins over contract, contract line, work item, and client default.
Unit: resolution depth by charge type — time and manual charges can reach the work-item step; usage, bucket, fixed, and project-schedule charges stop at the contract step.
Integration: migration creates exactly one system-managed default profile per existing client, and re-running the backfill creates no duplicates.
Integration: the single-default-per-client constraint rejects a second default profile.
Integration: phase-1 down migrations restore the prior schema and leave existing billing data intact.
Integration: client_billing_profiles is distributed correctly and is removed by tenant deletion.
Integration: every charge type writes a non-null billing_profile_id and billing_profile_source to invoice_charges during a full generation run.
Integration: project-schedule, sales-order, and invoice-modification charge paths all stamp a billing profile.
Integration: manual and ad-hoc invoice items persist a caller-supplied billing profile.
Regression: for a single-profile client, generated invoice totals, line amounts, and tax figures are byte-identical to pre-change output across the existing billing suite.
Integration scenario — multi-site group: N sites each with their own contract assigned to its own profile produce correctly segmented charges.
Integration scenario — shared site, multiple entities: one location carrying multiple profiles attributes charges by contract, not by location.
Integration scenario — one entity, multiple facilities: a single shared contract with no profile assignment attributes time charges by work item.
Integration: two time entries on tickets at different sites billed through the same hourly contract line resolve to different profiles, correcting the pre-existing coarse attribution.
Integration: a ticket's billing profile soft-defaults from the location default then the client default, and ticket creation succeeds when neither is set.
Integration: assigning a billing profile from another client to a ticket is rejected.
Integration: profile CRUD guards — archiving the default is rejected, and deleting a profile with charges is rejected in favor of archiving.
Component: no billing profile control renders on client, contract, contract line, ticket, or project surfaces while the client has one profile, and all appear once a second is added.
Integration: the spend-by-profile report totals match the sum of underlying invoice_charges, and drill-down returns exactly those charges.
Integration: the spend-by-profile report is unavailable for single-profile clients and is gated by its RBAC permission.
Integration: charges resolved via the client-default fallback are distinguishable from explicitly attributed charges in the report.
Integration: contract_line_source is recorded at time-entry create and at the generation-time reconcile path, with distinct values.
Integration: a time entry whose service matches more than one contract line is recorded as unresolved and appears in the review queue.
Integration: assigning a contract line from the unresolved queue clears the entry and updates its source value.
Component: the attribution inspector renders a distinct plain-language sentence for every billing_profile_source and contract_line_source value.
Integration: portal organization-wide spend equals the sum of per-profile spend, and per-profile invoice, ticket, and service views return only that profile's records.
Integration: the portal renders without a segment selector and identically to pre-change output for a single-profile client.
Integration: portal segment queries remain tenant-scoped and respect existing portal RBAC.
Integration: each profile-level billing field falls back to the client value when unset and overrides it when set.
Unit: tax region precedence resolves service region, then contract-line location region, then profile tax settings, then client default.
Integration: billing cycle backfill assigns every existing cycle to its client's default profile and the new unique constraint holds.
Integration: a client with multiple separately-billing profiles produces one cycle and one invoice document per profile, each with its own bill-to.
Integration: profiles with different billing frequencies generate cycles on their own schedules, and the mixed-currency guard applies per profile.
Integration: with the per-tenant feature flag off, cycle and invoice generation behave exactly as before the change.
Integration: payment methods are scoped per profile, backfilled rows land on the default profile, and default uniqueness holds per profile.
Integration: collecting payment for an invoice uses the payment method belonging to that invoice's profile and not a sibling profile's.
Integration: a credit issued against one profile cannot be applied to a sibling profile's invoice, and the derived balance reflects only its own profile.
Integration: aging and statements are produced per profile while client-level views sum correctly across profiles.

Integration: a separately-billing profile maps to a sub-customer under the client's parent customer, a single-profile client still maps to a plain customer, and invoice export targets the invoice profile's sub-customer.
Integration: a portal user restricted to a subset of profiles receives only permitted records and totals, enforced server-side even when the client requests another profile directly.
